'''Malevy Leons''' (born 23 September 1999) is a Dutch professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Mineral Area College#Athletics|Mineral Area College Cardinals]] and the [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley Braves]].

==Early career==
Leons was born and raised in [[IJmuiden]] by Iwan and Monique Leons and played in the youth academy of [[Apollo Amsterdam]]. He made his debut for the senior team in the [[Dutch Basketball League]] (DBL) during the [[2017–18 Dutch Basketball League|2017–18 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Basketballer Malevy Leons uit IJmuiden valt in Amerika in de prijzen [video]|url=https://www.noordhollandsdagblad.nl/cnt/dmf20210508_61714327|work=Noordhollands Dagblad|access-date=5 January 2022|language=nl-BE}}</ref> In the following season, Leons became a permanent member of the team and started in 15 games, contributing 5.9 points and 4 rebounds per game for Apollo.

==College career==
In 2019, Leons moved to the United States to play for [[Mineral Area College]] in [[Park Hills, Missouri]]. He helped the team claim a 20–0 record while winning the Midwest District championship. He led the team with 18.7 points and 9.5 rebounds, while also adding 2 blocks and 3.1 assists per game. Leons was named the [[NABC Player of the Year|Junior College Player of the Year]] by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] (NABC).<ref>{{cite news|title=Bradley Commit Malevy Leons Named Player of the Year |url=https://bradleybraves.com/news/2021/5/6/mens-basketball-bradley-commit-malevy-leons-named-player-of-the-year.aspx|work=Bradley University Athletics|date=6 May 2021|access-date=5 January 2022}}</ref>

Starting from the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]], Leons played for the [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley Braves]] in the [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC). He won back-to-back MVC Defensive Player of the Year awards in 2023 and 2024.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ersin|last=Demir|title=Malevy Leons Scouting Report|url=https://edemirnba.substack.com/p/malevy-leons-scouting-report|work=Ersin's NBA Draft Newsletter|date=18 May 2024|access-date=21 July 2024}}</ref> Leons averaged 13.8 points, 7.1 rebounds, 1.5 steals, 1.5 blocks and 1.3 assists per game as a fifth-year senior.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=Thunder rookie Malevy Leons posts monster stat line in G League game |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/rookie/2024/11/13/thunder-malevy-leons-okc-blue-g-league-stats/76258461007/ |access-date=5 January 2025 |work=Rookie Wire |date=13 November 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2024–2025)=== 
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Leons joined the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the [[NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Cody|last=Roskens|title=Malevy Leons signs with the Oklahoma City Thunder|url=https://bradleybraves.com/news/2024/6/27/mens-basketball-malevy-leons-drafted-by.aspx|website=BradleyBraves.com|date=27 June 2024|access-date=18 October 2024}}</ref> and on 27 September 2024, he signed with the team.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Thunder Sign Cormac Ryan, Two Others|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/thunder-sign-cormac-ryan-two-others.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=27 September 2024|access-date=28 September 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived on 19 October<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Minor Moves: Thunder, Raptors, Celtics, Lakers, Bucks|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/minor-moves-thunder-raptors-celtics-lakers-bucks.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=19 October 2024|access-date=19 October 2024}}</ref> and six days later, he joined the [[Oklahoma City Blue]]. On 31 October, he re-signed with the Thunder<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Malevy Leons|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder-signs-malevy-leons|website=NBA.com|date=31 October 2024|access-date=31 October 2024}}</ref> and on 1 November, Leons made his NBA debut against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], scoring one point and recording an assist and rebound each in three minutes played.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder 137-114 Trail Blazers (Nov 1, 2024) Game Recap|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401704706|website=ESPN.com|access-date=3 November 2024}}</ref> On 15 November, he was waived again by the Thunder<ref>{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Thunder Waive Malevy Leons|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/11/thunder-waive-malevy-leons.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=15 November 2024|access-date=16 November 2024}}</ref> and four days later, he joined the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=OKC BLUE|title=The Oklahoma City Blue has acquired forward/center Malevy Leons, the team announced today.|number=1859042727746314578|user=okcblue|date=19 November 2024|access-date=20 November 2024}}</ref>

On 30 July 2025, Leons re-signed with the Thunder on an [[Exhibit 10]] contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=OKC Thunder Ink Malevy Leons to Training Camp Deal|url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/okc-thunder-ink-malevy-leons-to-training-camp-deal|access-date=October 1, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref> He was waived prior to the start of the regular season on 18 October.<ref>{{cite web | last=Stiles | first=Rylan | title=OKC Thunder Ink Interesting Sharpshooter to Two-Way Pact | website=Oklahoma City Thunder On SI | date=2025-10-18 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/onsi/news/okc-thunder-ink-interesting-sharpshooter-to-two-way-pact | access-date=2025-12-05}}</ref>

===Golden State / Santa Cruz Warriors (2025–present)===
On December 8, 2025, Leons signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Warriors Sign Forward Malevy Leon’s to Two-Way Contract |url=https://warriors.com/news/warriors-sign-forward-malevy-leons-to-two-way-contract-20251208 |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=warriors.com |language=en}}</ref> In February 2026, Leons and fellow countryman [[Quinten Post]] became the first pair of Dutch teammates in the NBA since 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-03 |title=Post en Leons, ooit samen bij Apollo, nu teamgenoten in NBA: 'Het is absurd' |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2600799-post-en-leons-ooit-samen-bij-apollo-nu-teamgenoten-in-nba-het-is-absurd |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=nos.nl |language=nl}}</ref>

On 2 July, 2026, he joined the Warriors for the [[2026 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title= Warriors Announce Gold and Blue Rosters for California Classic |url= https://warriors.com/news/warriors-announce-gold-and-blue-rosters-for-california-classic-20260702 |website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2026|access-date=July 2, 2026}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Standing at {{convert|6|ft|9|in}} with a {{convert|7|ft|1|in|adj=on}} wingspan, scouts have praised his versatility for his size, as well as his defensive awareness.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ersin|last=Demir|title=Malevy Leons Scouting Report|url=https://edemirnba.substack.com/p/malevy-leons-scouting-report|work=Ersin's NBA Draft Newsletter|date=18 May 2024|access-date=21 July 2024}}</ref>
